entities.title: Control Cisco Secure Client/AnyConnect
entities.summary: Cisco Secure Client/AnyConnect is only observed through its tunnel routes; reading its state and reconnecting it are deferred.
entities.details: Today a tunnel from a client scutil does not manage is reported as UNSUPPORTED, and its faults get manual advice. The README marks AnyConnect control as deferred and the skill tells the agent that the user reconnects it.
acceptanceCriteria: The VPN check reports an AnyConnect tunnel's state instead of UNSUPPORTED.
fix --vpn can reconnect it, or the report says why it cannot (for example a sign-in it cannot do).
The README's Limitations and the skill's Rules are updated to match.

origin.description: Limitations: 'Other clients, including Cisco Secure Client/AnyConnect (deferred), are only observed through their tunnel routes.'

entities.title: Stale-route finding can name the same interface twice
entities.summary: routing() removes only adjacent duplicates from the interfaces of stale routes, so an interface whose stale routes are not next to each other in the table is named more than once.
entities.expected: The stale-routes finding and the Routing detail name each interface once, as Facts::tunnels does.
entities.observed: The names come from f.stale_routes() in table order and Vec::dedup drops only consecutive repeats; with stale routes on two interfaces interleaved (for example utun3's and utun5's IPv4 routes followed by their IPv6 routes) the finding reads 'utun3, utun5, utun3, utun5'.
reproduction: Build a snapshot with routes on utun3, utun5, utun3, utun5 in that order and neither interface up.
assess it and read the stale-routes finding's summary.

origin.description: Found by reading assess.rs while documenting the folder; not run.

entities.title: Two runs in the same second share a state directory
entities.summary: The state directory is named to the second and created with create_dir_all, so a second run started in the same second reuses the first run's directory.
entities.expected: Each run gets a fresh directory of its own, as Session::at's comment says.
entities.observed: The second run appends to the first run's diagnostic.log and overwrites its original.json, losing the first run's original settings.
reproduction: Start two fix-network runs within the same second with the same state root (for example from a script or an agent running them in parallel).
